newsitem.title: INDIA: India plans 1 bln-rupee trade aid for Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: India plans 1 bln-rupee trade aid for Bangladesh.

text.p: Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Thursday that India planned to extend aid worth 1.0 billion rupees ($27.9 million) to Bangladesh.

Deve Gowda told the Indian parliament in a statement after signing a landmark Ganges River water sharing treaty with visiting Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina that New Delhi planned more steps to consolidate bilateral trade ties.
"As the House would recall, we have already taken initiatives in the commercial sphere by extending tariff concessions to Bangladesh on a range of products of export interest to them," he said.
"We propose to extend commercial credits of 1.0 billion rupees to enhance trade relations further," he said.
Later Hasina told a joint news conference addressed by the two leaders that Bangladesh looked forward to more economic cooperation with India.
"Surely we can do more in areas of trade, technology and joint ventures," Hasina said.
She said liberalised economic policies in both South Asian countries had created conditions for closer economic cooperation.

"Great days are ahead of us," she said at the end of her statement lauding the water sharing treaty, under which India has agreed to evenly share water from a barrage on the Ganges during a lean March-May period when the water flow is low. ($1=35.89 rupees)
